plan.disposition: BUG intent never gets a mini-plan per the Phase Matrix (Mini-Plan row: FEATURE only at small); this run is a small BUG fix

findings.finding: _existing_fr_ids used fr_table_reader.read_active_fr_rows, which filters out rows under a '## Removed Requirements' heading. fr_table_reader's own docstring states a retired FR number must never be reused because removed rows still mean something to events.jsonl/the RTM/test tags/closed PRs. On regeneration of an adopted split whose spec.md has a retired FR row, the next QR id could silently collide with that retired id.
findings.suggestion: Use fr_table_reader.read_fr_rows (unfiltered, active+removed) in _existing_fr_ids instead of read_active_fr_rows, and add a regression test with a '## Removed Requirements' section holding a retired id in the range a naive scan would reuse.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a QR row's FR id can never collide with one something else still means, across any regeneration — generate_adoption_artifacts.py:363-365 assigns base-feature ids purely positionally (canonical_fr_id(i) for i=1..N over this run's freshly detected features), with no reference to existing_fr_ids. fold_features only guards the QR rows' OWN start position -- base's ids pass through untouched. If run 2 detects MORE features than run 1 (the growth direction, untested), a base feature's freshly assigned id can land on a number run 1's QR row occupied, silently repointing that id's meaning with no error.
findings.suggestion: either scope the guarantee down explicitly (this run's disposition: reasoned rebuttal), or thread existing_fr_ids into generate_adoption_artifacts.py's base-id assignment too (full fix, out of scope here).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: canonical_fr_id's overflow ValueError at position 9802 is safely unreachable — Confirmed uncaught -- would surface as a raw traceback mid-write rather than a clean message. Requires 9801+ detected features/QR rows in one split to reach.
findings.suggestion: not worth defensive handling for a condition this far from any real adopt run

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: write_spec's read-then-write of _existing_fr_ids has no TOCTOU risk — A real race exists in principle (read existing ids, then write, no lock) -- but adopt runs as a single orchestrated Claude Code session per split; nothing in this repo spawns two concurrent generate_adoption_artifacts.py processes against the same spec.md.
findings.suggestion: a lock only if adopt's invocation model ever becomes concurrent
